response.justification: The candidate is an experienced senior generalist software engineer, but the profile is almost entirely web/backend (TypeScript, Node.js, DLang, Ember, React) with only brief C/C++ exposure over a decade ago at National Instruments. The role requires strong C for UNIX development, Linux kernel investigation and source modification, embedded LAN-switch firmware, and specific security/networking domains (MACsec, 802.1X, L2/L3, SNMP, NETCONF, chip-vendor SDKs) — none of which appear in the resume. Critically, native-level Japanese proficiency is a hard requirement and the candidate lists only English, Romanian, and basic German, which alone disqualifies the application.
strengths: 15+ years of software development experience, well above the 3+ year minimum
Some low-level background: C/C++ work at National Instruments and C++/Linux/JACK audio thesis project
Strong engineering practices (TDD, CI/CD, DevOps, test tooling) and fluent English for technical documentation
concerns: No Japanese language ability, a stated native-level requirement
No embedded firmware, network switch, or Linux kernel modification experience
No demonstrated security domain expertise (MACsec, 802.1X, encryption, tamper detection) or L2/L3 networking

key_factors.factor: Lack of embedded/Linux kernel/C systems experience
Missing network security and switching domain knowledge
